grain.order_items: one row per order line item
grain.access_logs: one row per product page view

join_notes.access_logs: Fold case before joining: department_name and category_name are lowercase here and Title Case in order_items. After folding, all 6 departments match. Of 33 categories, 30 match and 3 do not: 'featured shops' and 'indoor outdoor games' have page views but no sales at all, and 'electronics' no longer matches because the fact table deliberately splits it into 'Electronics (Footwear)' and 'Electronics (Outdoors)' - join those two on category_id, never on the label. Of 76 products here, 72 match the fact table's 118, so 46 products have no page views and 4 page-viewed products were never ordered.

It is measured per line item: 0 of the 45,902 multi-item orders share one value, and profit == total x ratio holds row by row. SUM over all rows is correct; the source name would lead someone to de-duplicate by order_id and lose $2.58M.

fields.name: customer_zipcode
fields.business_description: US postal code of the customer, as 5 digits of text. Populated for every row; 995 distinct values.
fields.decision: Text, not integer: leading zeros are significant in US zipcodes - and the source has already lost them. 75,508 of 180,519 values (41.8%) are short because the field was stored as a number upstream: all 69,373 three-digit values are 603-983 in state PR (Puerto Rico's real range is 00601-00988) and all 6,135 four-digit values are 1201-8901 in CT, MA, NJ and RI (whose prefixes are 010-069). US zipcodes are exactly 5 digits, so zero-padding reconstructs the original and nothing else could. The pad is injective here - 995 distinct values before and after - so no two zipcodes collapse into one. Found by validation rule `zipcode_shape`.

fields.business_description: US postal code of the delivery address, as 5 digits of text. Null for non-US orders, which is most of them. The one fact column the vendor's glossary does not describe.
fields.decision: 86.2% blank, but not broken: populated for 24,840 of 24,840 rows whose order_country is Estados Unidos and blank for every non-US order. It is a US-only field, so it stays null elsewhere and is never imputed. Zero padded for the same reason as customer_zipcode - 1,087 four-digit values (1040-8901), every one in CT, ME, MA, NH, NJ, RI or VT, whose real prefixes are 010-089. Injective: 609 distinct values before and after.

fields.name: is_revenue_recognised
fields.decision: The most dangerous property of this dataset. 7,754 rows carrying $1,570,305.36 of order_item_sales never completed, yet they hold full sales and profit values. An unfiltered SUM(sales) overstates revenue by 4.27% ($36,784,735.01 -> $35,214,429.65) and SUM(profit) by 4.05%. This flag makes the filter explicit and hard to forget rather than leaving it to whoever writes the next query.

fields.name: is_shipment_valid
fields.decision: The same trap in the shipping columns. The 7,754 'Shipping canceled' rows still carry days_shipping_real, and those counters are residue: 4,423 of them read as late and 1,774 as early for shipments that never happened. late_delivery_risk agrees with delivery_status on every row but disagrees with (real > scheduled) on exactly those 4,423, so any delay or on-time-rate metric must filter on this flag first.
